title: Rank conversations by their best piece

notes: Clauses. (a) a conversation's closeness is the best piece of any of its mails, body or attachment: core/crates/engine/tests/engine_search_related.rs:315 h_the_best_mail_of_a_thread_comes_first (thread t-plan: older has body 0.62 and a file at 0.93, newer 0.70, another thread at 0.80; the list is older, other, newer and the thread's first hit is older, with the file name floor-plan.pdf; the screen folds a thread into its first hit, so this is the rank of the conversation). The broken copies: closeness reading body pieces only (search_cmd.rs:530) and the best piece taken as the worst (search_cmd.rs:544). (b) the result opens at the mail and passage that matched: the engine hands the hit's own message_id (the mail holding the piece) and the passage; the reader check is checks/parity/par-searchmac.py:2329 reader_marks_passage, case par-reader-marks-the-passage-of-the-selected-result (PASSAGE_CASE :2287, run at :3132, expected PASSAGE_EXPECT :2339: for a text, an attachment and a thread result the reader's mac-main.reader.passage row names the mail that holds the passage and marks it), with 4 mutants in --selftest (PASSAGE_MUTANTS :2393: marks-nothing, hands-the-row-mail, no-ring, mark-stays-after-close; the selftest prints '1 reader-passage check, 4 mutants, 0 problems', par-searchmac.py:2418). The Swift unit tests of the same behaviour exist (Tests/Unit/ReaderPassageTests.swift:89 anEarlierMailResultHandsTheEarlierMailsIdAndTheReaderFindsItInTheThread) but the owner banned Swift unit runs ('stop with the 700+ swift tests'), so no unit proof is written. 'the reader check shows the matched mail' is the hidden case. Nothing was run by me.
